context.requirement_text:
Second half of ISS-0431/GH#835's fix for its own stated PRIMARY
surface, atop REQ-216's core module. Mirrors REQ-186/REQ-187's and
REQ-214/REQ-215's own "core module first, wiring requirement(s)
second, disjoint files" split precedent in this file.

TWO ADMISSION GATES, NOT ONE, because tenant identity is not known
until partway through `Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline`'s existing chain --
read in full (lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex): `Plug.Parsers` runs
first, then `assign_trace_id`, then `Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline`
(which itself resolves tenant identity via a DB read -- token
verification, tenant-by-realm/slug resolution, JIT provisioning --
i.e. AuthPipeline's OWN work already consumes a DB connection BEFORE
any tenant identity exists to gate on), then
`Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`, then `match`/`dispatch`. Given that
ordering, a single per-tenant-only gate cannot run early enough to
cover AuthPipeline's own connection use. Resolved as follows, stated
as an accepted, disclosed limitation rather than silently glossed
over (matching this project's own honesty convention for a limitation
that cannot be fully closed within one requirement's scope, e.g.
decision 0014's own disclosed WASM native-crash gap):

1. GLOBAL gate, mounted FIRST in the chain -- before `Plug.Parsers`,
so a request rejected for lack of capacity is rejected before any
body-parsing work is spent on it. Calls
`Letflow.Admission.try_acquire(:global)`. Covers AuthPipeline's own
connection use (the gap named above) because it runs before
AuthPipeline and gates ALL downstream DB-connection-holding work,
auth included.
2. PER-TENANT gate, mounted immediately AFTER `Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline`
(tenant identity now resolved into `conn.assigns.auth_context.tenant_id`)
and BEFORE `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`/`match`/`dispatch`. Calls
`Letflow.Admission.try_acquire({:tenant, schema_name})`, resolving
`schema_name` the same way `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus` and
`Letflow.Scheduler.Poller` already do (tenant-id -> schema-name
resolution already exists in this codebase; reuse it, do not
re-derive). Covers TenantStatus's own DB lookup and every sub-router's
dispatch work -- the dominant share of connection-holding time per
REQ-056/ISS-0431's own round-trip profiling.
DISCLOSED LIMITATION: AuthPipeline's own DB work (steps 1-4 of its
moduledoc) is covered by the global gate only, not a per-tenant one,
because tenant identity does not exist yet at that point in the
chain. This is accepted, not silently omitted -- state it in this
plug's own moduledoc.
3. Both gates: on `{:error, :capacity}`, respond immediately (halt the
plug chain, no further plugs run) via
`Letflow.Api.Response.service_unavailable/2` (REQ-066, ALREADY
EXISTING -- do not add a new response helper), with the
`Retry-After` header set explicitly on the conn first (matching
`Response.rate_limited/2`'s own documented "caller sets Retry-After"
convention) to a fixed, configured seconds value (config, default 1)
-- NOT a computed estimate, since this admission mechanism has no
queueing/backoff-timing model to estimate from (a fixed short value
matching `Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus`'s own existing `@retry_after_seconds
"30"` precedent's SHAPE, though the specific number here is
independently justified: admission rejection is a near-instant
decision with no wait queue behind it, unlike TenantStatus's
migration-in-progress case, so a MUCH shorter retry-after is
appropriate -- state this reasoning in the plug's moduledoc rather
than copying TenantStatus's 30-second value uncritically).
4. On success at BOTH gates: the plug stores both `admission_ref()`s
in `conn.assigns` and registers a `Plug.Conn.register_before_send/2`
(or equivalent, matching how this codebase already threads
request-scoped cleanup -- state which mechanism is chosen and why) or
calls `Letflow.Admission.release/1` for both refs when the response is
sent, so an admitted request's slot is freed exactly once, on every
response path including a request that raises inside a downstream
plug or router (verified in the acceptance criteria below).
NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT: no change to REQ-216's core semaphore logic;
no change to `Letflow.Plugs.RateLimit` (still deferred, unmounted,
unrelated mechanism); no Poller wiring (REQ-218); no tier-weighted
per-tenant caps (REQ-216's own recorded open question).

task.description: RE-CHECK of ELIXIR-DEV's fix (step-04) for SECURITY-REVIEWER's own step-03 FAIL (double-global-consumption defect): verify the fix genuinely closes the finding, independently re-run the arithmetic, independently reproduce the mutation-test claim, and confirm nothing else regressed.

result.summary:
SCOPE TEST: applies (same as step-03 -- this diff wires plug behavior into the HTTP entry path). Re-ran the full INV-1..INV-9 pass is not needed since the fix diff (164490ab..HEAD) is scoped exactly to: (1) the new release_global_ref/1 function + moduledoc additions in lib/letflow/plugs/admission.ex, (2) the new :release_global_admission plug mount + moduledoc additions in lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex, (3) the design doc and test-file updates re-deriving AC3/AC4's minimum cap and adding two new proof tests, (4) handoff files. Confirmed via `git diff 164490ab..HEAD --stat`: 7 files touched, none outside this scope -- no new Ecto schema/migration/query, no new response field, no new outbound HTTP call, no new secret-resolution code. All of step-03's PASS findings (INV-4, INV-6, INV-7, INV-8, INV-9 NOT-APPLICABLE, auth-bypass safety, response-leak safety, process-dictionary cross-request-leak safety) are unaffected: release_global_ref/1 reuses the existing @admission_refs_pdict_key List.delete/2 + Process.put pattern and the existing Admission.release/1 call, matching the already-reviewed Mechanism A/B cleanup shape exactly, and touches only conn.assigns[:global_admission_ref] (this process's own prior ref, never tenant-suppliable, never a secret).

1. DIFF READ IN FULL (`git diff 164490ab..HEAD -- lib/letflow/plugs/admission.ex lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex`, prior commit found via `git log --oneline`, the commit at my own step-03 FAIL handoff). Confirmed: `plug(:release_global_admission)` is mounted between `plug(Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline)` and `plug(Letflow.Plugs.Admission, pool: :tenant)` in api_pipeline.ex (lines 118-133), delegating to `release_global_ref/1`. That function reads `conn.assigns[:global_admission_ref]` (nil -> no-op passthrough; present -> `Admission.release(ref)`, removes exactly that ref from the pdict list via `List.delete/2` (not a full clear -- the tenant ref, added later, is untouched), and sets the assign back to nil). This releases only the GLOBAL-only ref, never double-releases (the pdict deletion is targeted by value, and the assign is nilled so a second call is a safe no-op per the nil-check), and never releases the wrong ref (only :global_admission_ref is read, never :tenant_admission_ref).

2. ARITHMETIC RE-VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY by reading test/letflow/plugs/admission_pipeline_test.exs's AC3 (lines 166-197), AC4 (lines 200-245), and the two new proof tests (lines 274-327) directly, not trusting ELIXIR-DEV's comments. All four now run with `restart_admission!(pool_size: 1 or 2, reserved_headroom: 0 or 1)` i.e. global_cap == 1, and each asserts the request completes (404, not 503). This is only possible if the global gate's ref is freed before the tenant gate's own composing try_acquire({:tenant, schema}) consumes a global unit -- under the old (pre-fix) wiring, the tenant gate's call would see the global counter already at its cap-of-1 and reject with {:error, :capacity}, forcing 503. A single request therefore holds AT MOST ONE global unit at any instant under the fix, confirmed by direct derivation from the test assertions, not merely by reading the prose comments explaining them.

3. MUTATION TEST INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED BY ME (not trusting ELIXIR-DEV's reported numbers): edited lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex myself, commenting out `plug(:release_global_admission)`; ran `mix test test/letflow/plugs/admission_pipeline_test.exs` -- Result: 4/8 passed, 4 failed (AC3's 'cap of 1 concurrent request' test, AC4's 'a malformed :id' raise test, and both new proof tests 'global_cap == 1 admits one full request end to end' and 'at no instant during a single request's lifetime are two global units held simultaneously' -- all failing on `refute conn.status == 503` since conn1/conn.status == 503). This exactly matches ELIXIR-DEV's claimed mutation result (4 of 8 failing, the same four tests). Reverted the edit (`plug(:release_global_admission)` restored); `git status --short` showed a clean working tree after revert; reran the same test file -- Result: 8 passed, 0 failures. Confirmed genuinely non-vacuous: the failing tests were exactly and only the global_cap==1-dependent ones, not the whole suite.

4. REGRESSION SPOT-CHECK: `git diff 164490ab..HEAD --stat` confirms only the 7 scoped files changed -- no touch to Letflow.Router, Letflow.Api.Response, Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline, or any tenant-entity response-shaping code. Auth-bypass, response-leak, and process-dictionary cross-request-leak analysis from step-03 stands unchanged: the new plug only ever releases an admission ref and nils an assign -- it never halts, never dispatches, never mutates headers/body, and is unreachable except between AuthPipeline succeeding and the tenant gate running.

5. INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION COMMANDS, ALL RUN BY ME, FOREGROUND, REAL OUTPUT:
- `mix compile --warnings-as-errors --force` -> 'Compiling 184 files (.ex)' / 'Generated letflow app'. Zero warnings, zero errors.
- `mix format --check-formatted` -> no output, clean exit (all files already formatted).
- `mix test test/letflow/plugs/` -> 'Finished in 21.6 seconds' / 'Result: 113 passed', 0 failures.
- Mutation test (see point 3): 4/8 failed with the plug mount commented out, 8/8 passed after reverting -- reproduced myself, not trusted from the report.

VERDICT: PASS. The original double-global-consumption finding is genuinely closed -- a single request now holds at most one global admission unit at any instant, verified both by direct test-assertion re-derivation and by my own independently-reproduced mutation test. No new invariant violation introduced by the fix. Routing to REVIEWER for the OTP-idiom/scope gate.
